title: Unawareness of privacy implications during registration
description: The homeowner may not fully understand how their personal data and camera enrollment details will be used or shared by the Home Hub, leading to unintended privacy exposure.
assumptions: Homeowner is providing identifiable account and device information without detailed privacy notice review.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate based on typical LINDDUN Pro unawareness trees; exact subnode may vary.

title: Disclosure through insecure data storage on Home Hub
description: Upon receiving registration and enrollment data, the Home Hub process may store sensitive homeowner and sensor details in a way that allows unauthorized access or leaks.
assumptions: The process involves persisting account and camera enrollment data locally or in connected systems.

title: Linkability of homeowner identity via registration metadata
description: Data in transit during account registration and camera enrollment could use metadata (e.g., device identifiers, timing) to link the homeowner's actions across sessions or to their real-world identity.
assumptions: Registration flow transmits data over a network where metadata is observable.
uncertainty_note: Node id chosen as best fit for linkability in data flows; may need verification against full threat tree.

title: Guest unawareness of logging
description: Guest User may be unaware that entering the temporary access code results in the Home Hub logging the event, potentially associating it with their identity or visit details.
assumptions: The access code entry is processed and stored by the hub system.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate based on typical LINDDUN Pro unawareness category; exact tree not referenced from material.

title: Linkability via access code usage
description: Home Hub processing may enable linking the temporary code entry event to other data (e.g., time, door sensor) to identify or profile the guest's access patterns.
assumptions: Logs or data processing at P1 connect the code to identifiable context.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate; uncertain without full threat tree reference.

title: Detectability of code entry action
description: The data flow of entering the access code may make the guest's presence or action detectable through metadata or observation of the interaction with the Home Hub.
assumptions: Physical or local input could still be observed or logged in transit to processing.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate; flow is local input so detectability may not be strong.

title: Linkability of user activities via stored sensor events
description: The local event log stores timestamped motion/door/sensor events from the Home Hub, enabling linking of events to identify behavioral patterns or presence of specific individuals over time.
assumptions: Events include timestamps, sensor locations, and types that can be correlated.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate based on general LINDDUN knowledge without Pro reference material.

title: Identifiability of residents through event logs
description: Detailed sensor data in the log can uniquely identify individuals or households based on activity patterns, such as specific door usage or motion sequences.
assumptions: Log data is persistent and queryable by location/time.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate based on general LINDDUN knowledge without Pro reference material.

title: Disclosure of sensitive activity data from local storage
description: If the local event log is accessed (e.g., by unauthorized parties or malware), it discloses private information about home occupancy and routines.
assumptions: No or weak access controls on the datastore.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate based on general LINDDUN knowledge without Pro reference material.

title: Disclosure of video content containing personal data
description: Home Hub shares recorded camera clips that may include identifiable images of individuals, their activities, and private home environments to the cloud storage.
assumptions: Clips capture people and sensitive scenes without sufficient anonymization or consent checks at upload time.

title: Detectability of upload traffic revealing home activity
description: Metadata about the data flow (timing, volume, frequency of uploads) can be observed to detect presence or patterns of activity in the home.
assumptions: Traffic is not fully padded or anonymized, allowing traffic analysis.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate as exact LINDDUN Pro tree not referenced

title: Linkability of clips across time enabling profiling
description: Cloud storage links multiple video clips from the same home hub over time, allowing detailed behavioral profiling of residents.
assumptions: No pseudonymization or separation of storage for different clips/users.

title: Unawareness of data sharing implications
description: Users of the home hub may be unaware that video clips are being uploaded and stored in the cloud, including potential secondary uses.
assumptions: No clear notices or consent mechanisms at the device level before upload.

title: Disclosure of sensitive motion alert data during transmission
description: The real-time motion alert forwarded from the Home Hub to the Mobile App Backend may reveal private information about user presence, activities, or home occupancy if intercepted in transit.
assumptions: The alert contains timestamped motion data linked to a specific home/user account.
uncertainty_note: Exact payload contents and transport security (e.g., TLS) not specified in flow description.

title: Linkability of user activities via stored alerts
description: The backend may link successive motion alerts to build detailed profiles of inhabitant routines and presence patterns.
assumptions: Alerts are logged with user identifiers and timestamps for app notification history.

title: Detectability of motion notifications
description: Network observers can detect the push notification traffic, inferring when motion events occur at the property and potentially linking to homeowner activity patterns.
assumptions: Push notifications traverse observable networks without full traffic obfuscation.
uncertainty_note: Approximating LINDDUN Pro detectability node as D.1.1 due to lack of reference material; may be more specific like D.2.3 in Pro trees.

title: Disclosure of home security events
description: The notification may display or store details of motion detections on the homeowner's phone, which could be exposed to bystanders, family members, or if the device is lost/stolen.
assumptions: Notifications contain event details and are visible on lock screen or in history.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best guess without reference; could align with Dd.2 or similar for secondary disclosure.

title: Disclosure via inadequate aggregation
description: Sharing of aggregated device-usage analytics from the backend may inadvertently disclose individual user patterns if aggregation is insufficient or if data is re-identifiable.
assumptions: Aggregation techniques are applied but may have limitations
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate based on typical LINDDUN disclosure trees

title: Linkability through flow metadata
description: Metadata about the data flow between backend and analytics vendor could enable linking of app usage to specific vendor interactions.

title: Non-compliance with data minimization
description: Cloud analytics vendor may retain or process the received analytics beyond necessary purposes, violating privacy principles.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain on exact tree node for vendor-side compliance

title: Disclosure of sensitive video content in transit
description: The video clip retrieved from cloud storage to the backend may contain identifiable footage of the homeowner, family members, or visitors, and if transmitted without sufficient protection, metadata or content could be disclosed to unauthorized parties observing the flow.
assumptions: Assumes the video contains personal data and transmission is over public networks
uncertainty_note: Uncertain on exact LINDDUN Pro node for video disclosure in transit; using best guess for Dd.2.1

title: Linkability of video access to user identity
description: The mobile app backend, upon receiving the video from storage, can link the specific clip (with its timestamp, camera id, etc.) to the authenticated homeowner's account, enabling profiling of home activity patterns.
assumptions: Backend has access to user authentication context
uncertainty_note: Node id L.1.2 is approximate as no reference material; may relate to data item linkability

title: Unawareness of data sharing from storage
description: The cloud video storage shares the clip with the backend without the homeowner being fully aware of all internal retrievals or potential secondary uses by the backend service.
assumptions: Homeowner may not have detailed knowledge of backend data flows
